content.content: IEA reports utility-scale battery storage additions of about 70 GW in 2025, up 40% year on year, led by China, the United States and Europe. Four-hour lithium iron phosphate systems dominate new builds; the agency attributes the growth to falling pack prices and grid-services revenue.

NREL's 2025 benchmark puts LFP pack costs at about $95/kWh and installed four-hour system costs near $250/kWh, both down roughly 20% from 2024, with balance-of-system and interconnection now the largest cost shares.

BNEF projects cumulative grid-scale storage to pass 400 GWh by end-2025, notes long-duration pilots (iron-air, sodium-ion) reaching 100 MW scale, and flags interconnection queues as the main constraint on 2026 deployment.
